# NeuralNg Menu AI Context

Import canonical `NeuralMenu`, `NeuralMenuGroup`, `NeuralMenuItem`,
`NeuralMenuSeparatorItem`, and `NeuralMenuTrigger` only from
`@neural-ng/core/menu`. Legacy `*Component` and
`*Directive` exports are deprecated compatibility aliases.

Use `<neural-menu [items]="items">` for a flat inline command list. Use
`<neural-menu #menu="neuralMenu" popup>` with
`[neuralMenuTriggerFor]="menu"` for a popup command list.
Prefer attaching the trigger to `NeuralButton`; the directive resolves its
inner native button so ARIA and focus restoration stay on the interactive node.

Rules:

- Every action needs a stable unique `key` and a `label`.
- Use either `[items]` or projected `neural-menu-item` children, not both.
- Use `{ separator: true }` or `<neural-menu-separator />` for separators.
- Use `{ key, label, items }` or `<neural-menu-group key="..." label="...">`
  for non-interactive category headings. Group headings never receive focus.
- Handle commands through `(itemSelect)`; do not invent `onMenuClick`.
- Prefer `routerLink` for Angular SPA navigation and `href` for native or external navigation. Router items support queryParams, fragment, queryParamsHandling, preserveFragment, skipLocationChange, replaceUrl, state, and target.
- `[(open)]` is optional controlled popup state and produces `openChange`.
- `menuPosition` belongs on the trigger directive and defaults to
  `bottom-start`.
- Do not create a trigger for an inline Menu.
- Do not generate nested groups or submenus. A Menu group only categorizes a
  flat action sequence. Use PanelMenu for inline hierarchy and
  reserve popup nesting for the future TieredMenu.
- Prefer `iconClass="nt-user"`; NeuralNg adds the `nt` base class.
- `unstyled` removes visual classes while preserving behavior and structural
  hooks. Use typed `classes` slots for consumer styling.
- Popup Menu uses the shared Overlay positioner and browser Popover top layer.
- Preserve menu/menuitem semantics and built-in keyboard behavior.
